targets.body_template: **Experimenter-confirmed mapping correction.** The construct labels below supersede the earlier Test 2 labels. The source wells, RFU readings and endpoint calculations are unchanged; column 12 is Blank, whose composition is not documented. This is a relabelling of the same acquisition, not an independent experiment. ### What was measured Test 2 contains **72 observed wells**: six stimulus rows × twelve construct positions. Its archive key is `odor-2026-10-21`; the source exports record 21 October 2026 with no timezone. It is distinct from Test 1, the four-acquisition assay, and its column order must not be transferred from that assay. Rows B/C were not supplied here; they are not gain-based exclusions from this dataset. | Row | Addition | Supplied preparation | |---|---|---| | A | VUAA1 | 1:100 dilution | | D | Isopentyl acetate | 1:1,000 dilution | | E | 2-Heptanone | 1:1,000 dilution | | F | Valeric acid | 1:1,000 dilution | | G | Pentyl acetate | 1:1,000 dilution | | H | DMSO vehicle | 0.1% DMSO | The user reports 0.1% DMSO for the solutions. These preparation facts are retained as supplied; absolute molar concentrations cannot be inferred from dilution factors alone. The older assay's nominal VUAA1 concentration is not reused here. | Column | Condition | Corresponding composite | |---|---|---| | 1 | Or7a + ORCO | [BBa_26ZAGFK0](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26zagfk0#odor-2026-10-21) | | 2 | Or19a + ORCO | [BBa_2629NIWH](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-2629niwh#odor-2026-10-21) | | 3 | Or42a + ORCO | [BBa_26Q1Q094](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26q1q094#odor-2026-10-21) | | 4 | Or98a + ORCO | [BBa_26TZLBMJ](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26tzlbmj#odor-2026-10-21) | | 5 | Or22a + ORCO | [BBa_26WOX4B1](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26wox4b1#odor-2026-10-21) | | 6 | Or67a + ORCO | [BBa_265G8CE1](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-265g8ce1#odor-2026-10-21) | | 7 | Or67b + ORCO | [BBa_269VSDDR](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-269vsddr#odor-2026-10-21) | | 8 | Or59b + ORCO | [BBa_26Y7CI2H](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26y7ci2h#odor-2026-10-21) | | 9 | Or85b + ORCO | [BBa_26K1TU11](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26k1tu11#odor-2026-10-21) | | 10 | Or35a + ORCO | [BBa_26LLF3LM](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26llf3lm#odor-2026-10-21) | | 11 | ORCO only | [BBa_26E11Z80](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80#odor-2026-10-21) | | 12 | Blank | Composition not documented; no part assigned | ### Primary calculation: change within F1 minus change within F0 For each well, use the first and last actual reading in each acquisition: - **ΔF0 = 100 × [F0(48 s) / F0(0 s) − 1]**, in percent. - **ΔF1 = 100 × [F1(168 s) / F1(0 s) − 1]**, in percent. - **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). F0 has five readings at 12 s intervals and F1 has fifteen. This subtracts the observed baseline-stage disturbance from the observed within-F1 fluorescence change. It uses separate denominators for the two stages. No baseline line is extrapolated to 168 s, and no rate, peak value or mean F1/F0 ratio is substituted for these endpoints. The primary S windows are unequal: **48 s of F0 versus 168 s of F1**. Therefore the data also include **S48 = 100 × [F1(48 s)/F1(0 s) − 1] − ΔF0**, using equal 48 s windows. S48 is a sensitivity view of the recorded data, not an independent replicate or evidence that the longer-duration result is incorrect. The separate vehicle contrast is **S(stimulus,c) − S(H,c)**. A further blank-control contrast subtracts the corresponding vehicle contrast in column 12. These are differences between individual wells, with shared references; they remain dependent descriptive comparisons. Vehicle subtraction is additional to the primary within-well drift subtraction. ### Relation to Test 1 Test 1 had four acquisitions: a baseline before the blank addition, the blank round, a baseline before the test addition and the test round. Its retained calculation uses peak-three fluorescence changes and subtracts the blank-round excursion. Test 2 has only F0 and F1. **S is not the Test 1 R metric**, and these results are not pooled as replicated measurements of a single statistic. The Test 1 values remain unchanged and separately defined in their original tables. The mean-ratio metric **100 × (mean F1 / mean F0 − 1)** remains in the historical mean-ratio audit. It describes a different question and no longer supplies the main response conclusion. An F1 trajectory can rise even if its entire acquisition lies below the earlier F0 acquisition. Source timestamps do not identify the injection time, so no continuous injection-aligned trace is inferred. ### Reproducible inputs and limits There is one observed well per condition–addition pair. Five baseline readings and fifteen subsequent readings are within-well sampling, not twenty biological replicates. Numeric acquisition settings, stock molarities, addition-to-read delay and clone/culture lineage are not independently established from these exports. Within-stage normalization avoids making the between-acquisition level offset the response metric; it does not establish the biological cause of the trajectory. ### F1-only dynamics compared with DoOR The retained Test 2 F1 records were reanalysed using each well’s first-three and last-three mean (0/12/24 s and 144/156/168 s). D = L/E − 1 and C = D_odor − D_DMSO for the same supplied channel; 100C is reported in percentage points. This F1-only metric is distinct from F0-subtracted S and VUAA1-referenced N, and is a reanalysis rather than an independent experiment. The supplied F1 workbook channel mapping and source-cell provenance are retained. DoOR consensus minus receptor-specific spontaneous firing rate was compared with C separately for each odorant. Pearson r / Spearman rho: 2-heptanone +0.317/+0.406; isopentyl acetate +0.325/+0.442; valeric acid +0.211/+0.283; pentyl acetate −0.002/+0.006. n=10 receptors except valeric acid (n=9; missing Or42a reference). ORCO-only and blank controls are not included in tuning-OR correlations. Thus three odorants show weak positive correspondence and pentyl acetate is near zero. One well per condition and a shared vehicle reference constrain interpretation; positive C can mean less decline than DMSO. No independent replicate, significance claim, receptor-specific activation, or trained odor-classifier validation is inferred.
